extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and practitioners evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning and benchmarks
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running benchmark evaluations to measure large language models' capabilities and limitations on grade-school-level mathematical reasoning using controllable, symbolic question templates (GSM-Symbolic).

rubrics_metrics.name: GSM-Symbolic benchmark / symbolic templates
rubrics_metrics.description: GSM-Symbolic, an improved benchmark created from symbolic templates that allow for the generation of a diverse set of questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbolic templates to produce many controlled instantiations of the same problem structure, enabling more controllable evaluations and allowing systematic variation of elements (e.g., numeric values, clause structure) to probe model behavior and produce more reliable metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency across instantiations
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs exhibit noticeable variance when responding to different instantiations of the same question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate models on multiple instantiations of the same template and report variance/dispersion in performance, not just aggregate accuracy on a single instantiation, to assess consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to numeric variation
rubrics_metrics.description: The performance of all models declines when only the numerical values in the question are altered in the GSM-Symbolic benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure sensitivity by systematically changing numeric values in problems; large drops indicate poor generalization beyond memorized solution patterns tied to particular numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability / clause-count sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Model performance significantly deteriorates as the number of clauses in a question increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary the number of clauses in questions and quantify performance as clause_count grows to detect fragility in handling more complex, multi-clause logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to irrelevant / superficially relevant clauses (distractors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a single clause that seems relevant to the question causes significant performance drops (up to 65%) across all state-of-the-art models, even though the clause doesn't contribute to the reasoning chain needed for the final answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include distractor clauses that are superficially related but logically irrelevant to test whether models rely on genuine reasoning or are misled by plausibly related text; report performance degradation induced by such distractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of reported metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: It remains unclear whether reported improvements on benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K) reflect genuine advances in mathematical reasoning, raising questions about the reliability of the reported metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess metric reliability by using more controllable benchmarks (like GSM-Symbolic), measuring variance across instantiations and perturbations, and reporting sensitivity analyses rather than relying solely on single-shot aggregated scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing genuine logical reasoning from pattern replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesis: current LLMs cannot perform genuine logical reasoning; they replicate reasoning steps from their training data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct tests that minimize the chance of memorized patterns (e.g., novel combinations, unseen numeric instantiations, added distractors) to evaluate whether models truly perform logical inference versus reproducing learned solution templates.
